verses.zh: 又说：「当玛代王大利乌元年，我曾起来扶助米迦勒，使他坚强。
verses.en: “And in the first year of Darius the Mede, I[NOTE:1] stood to strengthen him and to provide protection for him.)
notes: The antecedent of the pronoun “I” is the angel, not Daniel. The traditional chapter division at this point, and the presence of a chronological note in the verse similar to ones used elsewhere in the book to position Daniel’s activities in relation to imperial affairs, sometimes lead to confusion on this matter.

verses.zh: 现在我将真事指示你：波斯还有三王兴起，第四王必富足远胜诸王。他因富足成为强盛，就必激动大众攻击希腊国。
verses.en: Now I will tell you the truth.“Three[NOTE:1] more kings will arise for Persia. Then a fourth[NOTE:2] king will be unusually rich,[NOTE:3] more so than all who preceded him. When he has amassed power through his riches, he will stir up everyone against[NOTE:4] the kingdom of Greece.
notes: Perhaps these three more kings are Cambyses (ca. 530-522 b.c.), Pseudo-Smerdis (ca. 522 b.c.), and Darius I Hystaspes (ca. 522-486 b.c.).
This fourth king is Xerxes I (ca. 486-465 b.c.).
Heb “rich with great riches.”

Or “All [of it] will arouse the kingdom of Greece.” The text is difficult. The text is traditionally taken to have the fourth king as the subject of the verb, making the relationship between הַכֹּל (hakkol, “all, the whole, everyone, everything”) and the kingdom of Greece difficult. Presumably “everyone” is the direct object, but the “kingdom” has the direct object marker אֶת (ʾet). This is very unlikely to be the preposition אֶת (ʾet, “with”) because the verb עוּר (ʿur, “to arouse”) uses the preposition עַל (ʿal) to mean “stir up against.” Nevertheless the meaning “against” is typically supplied or assumed from context. An alternative is to take הַכֹּל as the subject, meaning “all of it,” that is the power and wealth, will arouse [the interest] of the kingdom of Greece. This makes sense of the articular use of הַכֹּל, the parsing of the verb, and the direct object indicator, and also fits the context where in the next verse the Greek king rises up.

verses.zh: 必有一个勇敢的王兴起，执掌大权，随意而行。
verses.en: Then a powerful king[NOTE:1] will arise, exercising great authority and doing as he pleases.
notes: The powerful king mentioned here is Alexander the Great (ca. 336-323 b.c.).

verses.zh: 他兴起的时候，他的国必破裂，向天的四方（方：原文是风）分开，却不归他的后裔，治国的权势也都不及他；因为他的国必被拔出，归与他后裔之外的人。
verses.en: Shortly after his rise to power,[NOTE:1] his kingdom will be broken up and distributed toward the four winds of the sky[NOTE:2]—but not to his posterity or with the authority he exercised, for his kingdom will be uprooted and distributed to others besides these.
notes: Heb “and when he stands.”
Or “the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.

verses.zh: 南方的王必强盛，他将帅中必有一个比他更强盛，执掌权柄，他的权柄甚大。
verses.en: “Then the king of the south[NOTE:1] and one of his subordinates[NOTE:2] will grow strong. His subordinate[NOTE:3] will resist[NOTE:4] him and will rule a kingdom greater than his.[NOTE:5]
notes: The king of the south is Ptolemy I Soter (ca. 323-285 b.c.). The following reference to one of his subordinates apparently has in view Seleucus I Nicator (ca. 311-280 b.c.). Throughout the remainder of chap. 11 the expressions “king of the south” and “king of the north” repeatedly occur. It is clear, however, that these terms are being used generically to describe the Ptolemaic king (i.e., “of the south”) or the Seleucid king (i.e., “of the north”) who happens to be in power at any particular time. The specific identity of these kings can be established more or less successfully by a comparison of this chapter with the available extra-biblical records that discuss the history of the intertestamental period. In the following notes the generally accepted identifications are briefly mentioned.
Heb “princes.”
Heb “and he”; the referent (the subordinate prince mentioned in the previous clause) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “be strong against.”
Heb “greater than his kingdom.”

verses.zh: 过些年后，他们必互相连合，南方王的女儿必就了北方王来立约；但这女子帮助之力存立不住，王和他所倚靠之力也不能存立。这女子和引导她来的，并生她的，以及当时扶助她的，都必交与死地。
verses.en: After some years have passed, they[NOTE:1] will form an alliance. Then the daughter[NOTE:2] of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement, but she will not retain her power,[NOTE:3] nor will he continue[NOTE:4] in his strength.[NOTE:5] She, together with the one who brought her, her child,[NOTE:6] and her benefactor will all be delivered over at that time.[NOTE:7]
notes: Here they refers to Ptolemy II Philadelphus (ca. 285-246 b.c.) and Antiochus II Theos (ca. 262-246 b.c.).
The daughter refers to Berenice, who was given in marriage to Antiochus II Theos.
Heb “the strength of the arm.”
Heb “stand,” as also in vv. 7, 8, 11, 13.
Heb “and his arm.” Some understand this to refer to the descendants of the king of the north.
The present translation reads יַלְדָּה (yaldah, “her child”) rather than the MT יֹלְדָהּ (yoledah, “the one who begot her”). Cf. Theodotion, the Syriac, and the Vulgate.

Antiochus II eventually divorced Berenice and remarried his former wife Laodice, who then poisoned her husband, had Berenice put to death, and installed her own son, Seleucus II Callinicus (ca. 246-227 b.c.), as the Seleucid king.

verses.zh: 但这女子的本家（原文是根）必另生一子（子：原文是枝）继续王位，他必率领军队进入北方王的保障，攻击他们，而且得胜；
verses.en: “There will arise in his[NOTE:1] place one from her family line[NOTE:2] who will come against their army and will enter the stronghold of the king of the north and will move against them successfully.[NOTE:3]
notes: The reference is to the king of Egypt.
Heb “the stock of her roots.”sn The reference to one from her family line is probably to Berenice’s brother, Ptolemy III Euergetes (ca. 246-221 b.c.).
Heb “will deal with them and prevail.”

verses.zh: 并将他们的神像和铸成的偶像，与金银的宝器掠到埃及去。数年之内，他不去攻击北方的王。
verses.en: He will also take their gods into captivity to Egypt, along with their cast images and prized utensils of silver and gold. Then he will withdraw for some years from[NOTE:1] the king of the north.
notes: The Hebrew preposition מִן (min) is used here with the verb עָמַד (ʿamad, “to stand”). It probably has a sense of separation (“stand away from”), although it may also be understood in an adversative sense (“stand against”).

verses.zh: 北方的王（原文是他）必入南方王的国，却要仍回本地。
verses.en: Then the king of the north[NOTE:1] will advance against the empire of the king of the south, but will withdraw to his own land.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the king of the north) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 北方王（原文是他）的二子必动干戈，招聚许多军兵。这军兵前去，如洪水泛滥，又必再去争战，直到南方王的保障。
verses.en: His sons[NOTE:1] will wage war, mustering a large army that will advance like an overflowing river and carrying the battle all the way to the enemy’s[NOTE:2] fortress.[NOTE:3]
notes: The sons of Seleucus II Callinicus were Seleucus III Ceraunus (ca. 227-223 b.c.) and Antiochus III the Great (ca. 223-187 b.c.).
Heb “his”; the referent (the enemy of the king of the north) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and he will certainly come and overflow and cross over and return and be aroused unto a fortress.” The translation has attempted to simplify the syntax of this difficult sequence.

verses.zh: 南方王必发烈怒，出来与北方王争战，摆列大军；北方王的军兵必交付他手。
verses.en: “Then the king of the south[NOTE:1] will be enraged and will march out to fight against the king of the north, who will also muster a large army, but that army will be delivered into his hand.
notes: This king of the south refers to Ptolemy IV Philopator (ca. 221-204 b.c.).

verses.zh: 他的众军高傲，他的心也必自高；他虽使数万人仆倒，却不得常胜。
verses.en: When the army is taken away, the king of the south will become arrogant.[NOTE:1] He will be responsible for the death[NOTE:2] of thousands and thousands of people,[NOTE:3] but he will not continue to prevail.
notes: Heb “his heart will be lifted up.” The referent (the king of the south) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “cause to fall.”
Heb “of myriads.”

verses.zh: 北方王必回来摆列大军，比先前的更多。满了所定的年数，他必率领大军，带极多的军装来。
verses.en: For the king of the north will again muster an army, one larger than before. At the end of some years he will advance with a huge army and enormous supplies.

verses.zh: 那时，必有许多人起来攻击南方王，并且你本国的强暴人必兴起，要应验那异象，他们却要败亡。
verses.en: “In those times many will oppose[NOTE:1] the king of the south.[NOTE:2] Those who are violent[NOTE:3] among your own people will rise up in confirmation of[NOTE:4] the vision, but they will falter.
notes: Heb “stand against.”
This was Ptolemy V Epiphanes (ca. 203-181 b.c.).

Heb “sons of violence.” “Son(s)” is sometimes used idiomatically in Hebrew to indicate that someone is characterized by a certain quality. So the expression “sons of violence” means that these individuals will be characterized by violent deeds.
Heb “to cause to stand.”

verses.zh: 北方王必来筑垒攻取坚固城；南方的军兵必站立不住，就是选择的精兵（原文是民）也无力站住。
verses.en: Then the king of the north will advance and will build siege mounds and capture a well-fortified city.[NOTE:1] The forces of the south will not prevail, not even his finest contingents.[NOTE:2] They will have no strength to prevail.
notes: This well-fortified city is apparently Sidon. Its capture from the Ptolemies by Antiochus the Great was a strategic victory for the Seleucid kingdom.
Or “choice troops” (BDB 104 s.v. מִבְחָר), or “elite troops” (HALOT 542 s.v. מִבְחָר).

verses.zh: 来攻击他的，必任意而行，无人在北方王（原文是他）面前站立得住。他必站在那荣美之地，用手施行毁灭。
verses.en: The one advancing against him will do as he pleases, and no one will be able to stand before him. He will prevail in the beautiful land, and its annihilation will be within his power.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 他必定意用全国之力而来，立公正的约，照约而行，将自己的女儿给南方王为妻，想要败坏他（或译：埃及），这计却不得成就，与自己毫无益处。
verses.en: His intention[NOTE:1] will be to come with the strength of his entire kingdom, and he will form alliances.[NOTE:2] He will give the king of the south[NOTE:3] a daughter[NOTE:4] in marriage in order to destroy the kingdom, but it will not turn out to his advantage.
notes: Heb “and he will set his face” (cf. vv. 18, 19).
The present translation reads מֵישָׁרִים (mesharim, “alliances”) for the MT וִישָׁרִים (viysharim, “uprightness”).
Heb “him”; the referent (the king of the south) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the daughter of the women.”sn The daughter refers to Cleopatra, the daughter of Antiochus, who was given in marriage to Ptolemy V.

verses.zh: 其后他必转回夺取了许多海岛。但有一大帅，除掉他令人受的羞辱，并且使这羞辱归他本身。
verses.en: Then he will turn his attention[NOTE:1] to the coastal regions and will capture many of them. But a commander[NOTE:2] will bring his shameful conduct to a halt; in addition,[NOTE:3] he will make him pay for his shameful conduct.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “his face,” as also in v. 19.
The commander is probably the Roman commander, Lucius Cornelius Scipio.
The Hebrew here is difficult in that the negative בִּלְתִּי (bilti, “not”) is used in an unusual way. The sense is not entirely clear.
Heb “his shameful conduct he will return to him.”

verses.zh: 他就必转向本地的保障，却要绊跌仆倒，归于无有。
verses.en: He will then turn his attention to the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall, not to be found again.

verses.zh: 那时，必有一人兴起接续他为王，使横征暴敛的人通行国中的荣美地。这王不多日就必灭亡，却不因忿怒，也不因争战。
verses.en: There will arise after him[NOTE:1] one[NOTE:2] who will send out an exactor[NOTE:3] of tribute to enhance the splendor of the kingdom, but after a few days he will be destroyed,[NOTE:4] though not in anger or battle.
notes: Heb “on his place.”
The one who will send out an exactor of tribute was Seleucus IV Philopator (ca. 187-176 b.c.).
Perhaps this exactor of tribute was Heliodorus (cf. 2 Macc 3).
Heb “broken” or “shattered.”

verses.zh: 必有一个卑鄙的人兴起接续为王，人未曾将国的尊荣给他，他却趁人坦然无备的时候，用谄媚的话得国。
verses.en: “Then there will arise in his place a despicable person[NOTE:1] to whom the royal honor has not been rightfully conferred. He will come on the scene in a time of prosperity and will seize the kingdom through deceit.
notes: This despicable person to whom the royal honor has not been rightfully conferred is Antiochus IV Epiphanes (ca. 175-164 b.c.).

verses.zh: 必有无数的军兵势如洪水，在他面前冲没败坏；同盟的君也必如此。
verses.en: Armies[NOTE:1] will be suddenly[NOTE:2] swept away in defeat[NOTE:3] before him; both they and a covenant leader[NOTE:4] will be destroyed.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “arms.”
The present translation reads הִשָּׁטֹף (hishatof), Niphal infinitive absolute of שָׁטַף (shataf, “to overflow”), for the MT הַשֶּׁטֶף (hashetef, “flood”).
The words “in defeat” are added in the translation for clarification.
Heb “a prince of the covenant.”
Heb “broken” or “shattered.”

verses.zh: 与那君结盟之后，他必行诡诈，因为他必上来以微小的军（原文是民）成为强盛。
verses.en: After[NOTE:1] entering into an alliance with him, he will behave treacherously; he will ascend to power with only a small force.[NOTE:2]
notes: The preposition מִן (min) is probably temporal here (so BDB 583 s.v. 7.c; cf. KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV), although it could also be understood here as indicating means (so J. Goldingay, Daniel [WBC], 279, n. 23a; cf. TEV, NLT).
Heb “nation.”

verses.zh: 趁人坦然无备的时候，他必来到国中极肥美之地，行他列祖和他列祖之祖所未曾行的，将掳物、掠物，和财宝散给众人，又要设计攻打保障，然而这都是暂时的。
verses.en: In a time of prosperity for the most productive areas of the province, he will come and accomplish what neither his fathers nor their fathers accomplished. He will distribute loot, spoils, and property to his followers, and he will devise plans against fortified cities, but not for long.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and unto a time.”

verses.zh: 他必奋勇向前，率领大军攻击南方王；南方王也必以极大极强的军兵与他争战，却站立不住，因为有人设计谋害南方王。
verses.en: He will rouse his strength and enthusiasm[NOTE:1] against the king of the south[NOTE:2] with a large army. The king of the south will wage war with a large and very powerful army, but he will not be able to prevail because of the plans devised against him.
notes: Heb “heart.”
This king of the south was Ptolemy Philometer (ca. 181-145 b.c.).

verses.zh: 吃王膳的，必败坏他；他的军队必被冲没，而且被杀的甚多。
verses.en: Those who share the king’s fine food will attempt to destroy him, and his army will be swept away;[NOTE:1] many will be killed in battle.
notes: The present translation reads יִשָׁטֵף (yishatef, passive) rather than the MT יִשְׁטוֹף (yishtof, active).

verses.zh: 至于这二王，他们心怀恶计，同席说谎，计谋却不成就；因为到了定期，事就了结。
verses.en: These two kings, their minds[NOTE:1] filled with evil intentions, will trade[NOTE:2] lies with one another at the same table. But it will not succeed, for there is still an end at the appointed time.
notes: Heb “heart,” as also in v. 28.
Heb “speak.”

verses.zh: 北方王（原文是他）必带许多财宝回往本国，他的心反对圣约，任意而行，回到本地。
verses.en: Then the king of the north[NOTE:1] will return to his own land with much property. His mind will be set against the holy covenant. He will take action, and then return to his own land.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the king of the north) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 到了定期，他必返回，来到南方。后一次却不如前一次，
verses.en: At an appointed time he will again invade the south, but this latter visit will not turn out the way the former one did.

verses.zh: 因为基提战船必来攻击他，他就丧胆而回，又要恼恨圣约，任意而行；他必回来联络背弃圣约的人。
verses.en: The ships of Kittim[NOTE:1] will come against him, leaving him disheartened.[NOTE:2] He will turn back and direct his indignation against the holy covenant. He will return and honor[NOTE:3] those who forsake the holy covenant.
notes: The name Kittim has various designations in extra-biblical literature. It can refer to a location on the island of Cyprus, or more generally to the island itself, or it can be an inclusive term to refer to parts of the Mediterranean world that lay west of the Middle East (e.g., Rome). For ships of Kittim the Greek OT (LXX) has “Romans,” an interpretation followed by a few English versions (e.g., TEV). A number of times in the Dead Sea Scrolls the word is used in reference to the Romans. Other English versions are more generic: “[ships] of the western coastlands” (NIV, NLT); “from the west” (NCV, CEV).

This is apparently a reference to the Roman forces, led by Gaius Popilius Laenas, which confronted Antiochus when he came to Egypt and demanded that he withdraw or face the wrath of Rome. Antiochus wisely withdrew from Egypt, albeit in a state of bitter frustration.
Heb “show regard for.”

verses.zh: 他必兴兵，这兵必亵渎圣地，就是保障，除掉常献的燔祭，设立那行毁坏可憎的。
verses.en: His forces[NOTE:1] will rise up and profane the fortified sanctuary,[NOTE:2] stopping the daily sacrifice. In its place they will set up[NOTE:3] the abomination that causes desolation.
notes: Heb “arms.”
Heb “the sanctuary, the fortress.”
Heb “will give.”

verses.zh: 作恶违背圣约的人，他必用巧言勾引；惟独认识　神的子民必刚强行事。
verses.en: Then with smooth words he will defile[NOTE:1] those who have rejected[NOTE:2] the covenant. But the people who are loyal to[NOTE:3] their God will act valiantly.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “corrupt.”
Heb “acted wickedly toward.”
Heb “know.” The term “know” sometimes means “to recognize.” In relational contexts it can have the connotation “recognize the authority of, be loyal to,” as it does here.
This is an allusion to the Maccabean revolt, which struggled to bring about Jewish independence in the second century b.c.

verses.zh: 民间的智慧人必训诲多人；然而他们多日必倒在刀下，或被火烧，或被掳掠抢夺。
verses.en: These who are wise among the people will teach the masses.[NOTE:1] However, they will fall[NOTE:2] by the sword and by the flame,[NOTE:3] and they will be imprisoned and plundered for some time.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the many.”
Heb “stumble.”
Or “by burning.”
Heb “days.”

verses.zh: 他们仆倒的时候，稍得扶助，却有许多人用谄媚的话亲近他们。
verses.en: When they stumble, they will be granted some help. But many will unite with them deceitfully.

verses.zh: 智慧人中有些仆倒的，为要熬炼其余的人，使他们清净洁白，直到末了；因为到了定期，事就了结。
verses.en: Even some of the wise will stumble, resulting in their refinement, purification, and cleansing until the time of the end, for it is still for the appointed time.

verses.zh: 王必任意而行，自高自大，超过所有的神，又用奇异的话攻击万神之神。他必行事亨通，直到主的忿怒完毕，因为所定的事必然成就。
verses.en: “Then the king[NOTE:1] will do as he pleases. He will exalt and magnify himself above every deity, and he will utter presumptuous things against the God of gods. He will succeed until the time of[NOTE:2] wrath is completed, for what has been decreed must occur.[NOTE:3]
notes: The identity of this king is problematic. If vv. 36-45 continue the description of Antiochus Epiphanes, the account must be viewed as erroneous, since the details do not match what is known of Antiochus’ latter days. Most modern scholars take this view, concluding that this section was written just shortly before the death of Antiochus and that the writer erred on several key points as he tried to predict what would follow the events of his own day. Conservative scholars, however, usually understand the reference to shift at this point to an eschatological figure, viz., the Antichrist. The chronological gap that this would presuppose to be in the narrative is not necessarily a problem, since by all accounts there are many chronological gaps throughout the chapter, as the historical figures intended by such expressions as “king of the north” and “king of the south” repeatedly shift.
The words “the time of” are added in the translation for clarification.
Heb “has been done.” The Hebrew verb used here is the perfect of certitude, emphasizing the certainty of fulfillment.

verses.zh: 他必不顾他列祖的神，也不顾妇女所羡慕的神，无论何神他都不顾；因为他必自大，高过一切。
verses.en: He will not respect[NOTE:1] the gods of his fathers—not even the god loved by women.[NOTE:2] He will not respect any god; he will elevate himself above them all.
notes: Heb “consider.”
Heb “[the one] desired by women.” The referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他倒要敬拜保障的神，用金、银、宝石和可爱之物敬奉他列祖所不认识的神。
verses.en: What he will honor is a god of fortresses—a god his fathers did not acknowledge he will honor with gold, silver, valuable stones, and treasured commodities.

verses.zh: 他必靠外邦神的帮助，攻破最坚固的保障。凡承认他的，他必将荣耀加给他们，使他们管辖许多人，又为贿赂分地与他们。
verses.en: He will attack[NOTE:1] mighty fortresses, aided by[NOTE:2] a foreign deity. To those who recognize him he will grant considerable honor. He will place them in authority over many people, and he will parcel out land for a price.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “act against.”
Heb “with.”
Or perhaps “for a reward.”

verses.zh: 到末了，南方王要与他交战。北方王必用战车、马兵，和许多战船，势如暴风来攻击他，也必进入列国，如洪水泛滥。
verses.en: “At the time of the end the king of the south will attack[NOTE:1] him. Then the king of the north will storm against him[NOTE:2] with chariots, horsemen, and a large armada of ships.[NOTE:3] He[NOTE:4] will invade lands, passing through them like an overflowing river.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “engage in thrusting.”
The referent of the pronoun is most likely the king of the south, in which case the text describes the king of the north countering the attack of the king of the south.
Heb “many ships.”
This most likely refers to the king of the north who, in response to the aggression of the king of the south, launches an invasion of the southern regions.
Heb “and will overflow and pass over.”

verses.zh: 又必进入那荣美之地，有许多国就被倾覆，但以东人、摩押人，和一大半亚扪人必脱离他的手。
verses.en: Then he will enter the beautiful land.[NOTE:1] Many[NOTE:2] will fall, but these will escape:[NOTE:3] Edom, Moab, and the Ammonite leadership.
notes: The beautiful land is a cryptic reference to the land of Israel.
This can be understood as “many people” (cf. NRSV) or “many countries” (cf. NASB, NIV, NLT).
Heb “be delivered from his hand.”

verses.zh: 他必伸手攻击列国；埃及地也不得脱离。
verses.en: He will extend his power[NOTE:1] against other lands; the land of Egypt will not escape.
notes: Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 他必把持埃及的金银财宝和各样的宝物。利比亚人和古实人都必跟从他。
verses.en: He will have control over the hidden stores of gold and silver, as well as all the treasures of Egypt. Libyans and Ethiopians[NOTE:1] will submit to him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “Nubians” (NIV84, NCV); Heb “Cushites” (NIV11).
Heb “Libyans and Cushites [will be] at his footsteps.”

verses.zh: 但从东方和北方必有消息扰乱他，他就大发烈怒出去，要将多人杀灭净尽。
verses.en: But reports will trouble him from the east and north, and he will set out in a tremendous rage to destroy and wipe out many.

verses.zh: 他必在海和荣美的圣山中间设立他如宫殿的帐幕；然而到了他的结局，必无人能帮助他。
verses.en: He will pitch his royal tents between the seas[NOTE:1] toward the beautiful holy mountain. But he will come to his end, with no one to help him.
notes: Presumably seas refers to the Mediterranean Sea and the Dead Sea.
